page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores running at a base clock of 3.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, delivering 4.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not included, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. The network interface features a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and no dedicated GPU hardware is attached.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate balanced single-core execution alongside constrained multi-core capacity under sustained load. The instance achieved average ratings in PassMark CPU (7332.31) and Geekbench single-core (1892.0), bolstered by strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression (32.91 GB/sec) and Geekbench text processing (2498.0). Conversely, multi-core metrics fall into lower percentiles due to its burstable 2-core physical configuration, scoring 3944.96 in stress-ng multi-core and 4435.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Large-block uncached memory read throughput reached 26.17 GB/sec, placing it in the lower quartile of tested configurations.

Given its burstable CPU allocation and 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the m7i-flex.xlarge serves as a cost-efficient profile for moderate general-purpose services that do not constantly saturate all execution threads. It handles static web serving (measured at 7.35 GB/sec) and lightweight text-oriented background tasks reliably. However, operations with intensive concurrent requirements, such as high-concurrency database queries, Clang compilation, or continuous multi-threaded decompression, experience noticeable performance limitations on this tier.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. Supported by the Nitro hypervisor, it provides 16.0 GB of DDR5 RAM, 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not include local disk storage or GPU acceleration. In benchmark assessments, the instance achieves competitive single-core execution, demonstrated by strong single-threaded gzip compression at 32.91 GB/sec and average single-core Geekbench marks of 1892.0. However, multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth register lower results, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 4435.0 and PassMark database operations scoring 2063.13. The m7i-flex.xlarge offers cost efficiency for workloads with fluctuating CPU demands, making it appropriate for static web serving, mid-tier application hosting, and lightweight batch processing rather than sustained high-throughput computational or database tasks.
